transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work. I'm a buyer, and... I don't know. I just can't shake this feeling that people there, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys. Like they're... messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor showed me the reports and says they don't prove anything like that is happening, but... yeah. I just can't shake it. So I'm here.
How long have you been feeling this way about people tracking your buys and messing with the numbers—days, weeks, or longer?
Um... longer. I guess it's been... roughly ten months now. That's when I started noticing what they were doing. And... when the voice started, too.
Can you tell me more about this voice you mentioned—what does it say, and do you hear it as if someone is actually speaking, separate from your own thoughts?

Yeah... it sounds real. Like an actual person, not just in my head. 

It's a guy's voice. Um... usually I hear it when I'm alone in the stockroom, or if I'm driving back from a vendor meeting. It sounds like it's coming from right behind me. He just... he says things like, "Move faster, Scott." Or he just laughs at my picks. 

But... when I turn around, nobody's there.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs during this time?
Um... no. I don't... I don't really do any of that stuff.
During these past ten months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or on the other hand unusually high, energetic, or irritable, lasting days or weeks?

Um... yeah, I guess. Not really low or hopeless, but... sometimes I get these stretches where I just feel... I don't know, like the whole city is opening up for me. Like everything is just clicking. 

But then... if someone at work questions a purchase order, or tells me I need to slow down... I get really mad. Like, I snap at them way harder than I mean to. It just... it just happens.

During the times when you don't feel that high, energetic sense of things 'clicking' or the irritability—like when your mood feels more normal—do you still hear that voice or still feel like people are tracking and messing with your buys?

Yeah... I mean, even when I'm not feeling like that... like when things are just normal and I'm actually sleeping... it doesn't stop. 

There was a stretch a while back... a few weeks where I was pretty calm. But I still... I still knew people were messing with my orders. And I still heard him in the stockroom. It didn't go away.
When you have those stretches of feeling like everything is 'clicking' and you're more irritable, how long do those periods usually last—days, a week, or longer?
I don't really count the days. Um... but those stretches... the high-energy ones where I get like that... they've been happening for about eleven months now.
Over the full ten months since this all started, would you say you've been in one of those high-energy, irritable stretches most of the time, or has it been more of a smaller portion of that time?

Um... yeah, I guess. If I look back... it's been mostly that way. 

Most of the time since this all started, I've just been... wired, I guess. Working too much, feeling like I knew better than everyone else, getting mad when they tried to slow me down. 

There were some calmer parts, but... they were shorter. Mostly it's just been those high-energy stretches.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports ~10-11 months of persecutory delusions (belief that coworkers/vendors are tracking and sabotaging his buys) and auditory hallucinations (a male voice commenting/laughing at him, heard as external), with no substance use or medical cause. Concurrently, he describes a prolonged manic-like syndrome (elevated, expansive mood 'city opening up,' increased goal-directed work activity, irritability, decreased need to slow down) that has been present for the majority of the illness duration (~most of 10-11 months). Critically, there was a distinct period of several weeks where mood symptoms remitted (calm, euthymic) yet the psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisted, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of mood episode for at least 2 weeks. The combination of a manic episode overlapping with psychotic symptoms for the majority of the illness, plus psychotic symptoms persisting for ≥2 weeks without mood symptoms, supports Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0) over Schizophrenia (mood symptoms too prominent/prolonged) or Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (psychotic symptoms outlast mood episodes).
